questions.q: Per this lesson, what three operational questions does Snowflake governance answer for every query?
options: Who can see this, what do they see once allowed, and what gets tracked when they look
How fast is the query, how much does it cost, and who wrote it
Which warehouse ran it, how long it took, and whether it was cached
Is the data fresh, is it backed up, and is it replicated
questions.explain: Governance in Snowflake is operational, not a policy document — it governs access, what's visible once access is granted, and auditability.

questions.q: Where does the Governance tab live in Snowsight's navigation?
options: Under Admin, next to Billing & Terms
Under Monitoring, alongside Query History and Task History
It isn't in the UI — it's SQL-only
Under Data, next to Databases
questions.explain: Governance sits as its own tab under Monitoring, right beside Query History — a first-class part of the platform, not a separate product.

options: A separate product you must purchase and provision before governance features work
Snowflake's umbrella branding for its built-in governance capabilities like tagging, masking, and access history
The name of Snowflake's query optimizer
A third-party governance add-on that integrates with Snowflake
questions.explain: Horizon is Snowflake's own name for the governance capability already built into the platform — not a bolt-on product.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three pillars this course is organized around?
options: Access control
Data protection
Tags and classification
Data warehouse performance tuning
questions.explain: The three pillars are access control (who), data protection (what they see), and tags/classification (the metadata layer driving the first two at scale). Performance tuning isn't a governance pillar.

questions.q: In the TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS example shown, why does tagging columns with TASTY_PII matter rather than writing a separate masking policy per column?
options: It makes queries run faster
It lets one policy attached to the tag apply to every column carrying that tag, including future ones, instead of one policy per column
Tags are required by SQL syntax for any SELECT statement
It automatically deletes the tagged columns
questions.explain: Tagging is the metadata layer: attach a policy to a tag once, and it governs every column (current and future) that carries that tag — this is exactly what Chapter 3 builds on.
